title: Cloud Atlas
events_chronological: 1849: American lawyer Adam Ewing, sailing home across the Pacific, watches the slave trade at work while the doctor Henry Goose quietly poisons him for his gold.
1849: the stowaway slave Autua, whose life Ewing saved, nurses him through the poisoning and exposes Goose.
1849: Ewing returns to San Francisco and renounces his father-in-law's slaving fortune to join the abolitionists.
1936: penniless composer Robert Frobisher talks his way into the household of the ailing Vyvyan Ayrs as his amanuensis, writing constantly to his lover Rufus Sixsmith.
1936: Frobisher finds half of Ewing's journal in the Zedelghem library and writes the Cloud Atlas Sextet while Ayrs tries to claim it as his own.
1936: Frobisher finishes the Sextet, shoots himself in a Bruges hotel bath, and Sixsmith arrives too late.
1973: journalist Luisa Rey is trapped in a stalled lift with the elderly Sixsmith, who tells her about a suppressed safety report on the Swannekke nuclear plant.
1973: Sixsmith is murdered, Luisa inherits Frobisher's letters to him, and the hitman Bill Smoke runs her car off a bridge.
1973: Luisa and the engineer Isaac Sachs's report bring the conspiracy down and she publishes the story.
2012: publisher Timothy Cavendish, hunted by an author's gangster brothers, is tricked by his own brother into signing himself into the Aurora House nursing home.
2012: drugged and locked in, Cavendish reads the Luisa Rey manuscript and organises an escape with three fellow residents.
2012: the escapees fight their way out through a pub full of Scots, and Cavendish writes his ordeal up as a screenplay.
2144: the fabricant server Sonmi-451 is lifted out of Papa Song's diner by the rebel Hae-Joo Chang and shown what the world outside is.
2144: Sonmi watches the Cavendish film, learns that spent fabricants are recycled into food for the living, and records a declaration of her rights.
2144: Sonmi is captured and executed, and her declaration survives her as scripture.
After the Fall: the goatherd Zachry, whose tribe worships Sonmi as a god, guides the technologically advanced Meronym up to the mountain observatory while the Kona raid his valley.
After the Fall: Zachry ignores the whispering demon Old Georgie, kills a Kona warrior, and Meronym sends the signal that will bring a ship.
Off world: an aged Zachry tells his grandchildren the whole story under an alien sky, with Meronym beside him.
syuzhet_notes: Six stories spread across five centuries are cut into one another continuously, often on a matched gesture or a shared line, so consecutive told-order bullets are usually decades or centuries apart. The film opens on its chronologically last scene (told-order bullet 1) as a framing narration, makes one pass through all six eras in bullets 2-7, then cycles through them twice more, and closes on its earliest era at bullet 18.
fabula_notes: The eras are separated by centuries with no continuous causal chain, so the chronology is ordered by date rather than by consequence; what actually links them is a document handed forward - Ewing's journal, Frobisher's letters, Luisa's manuscript, Cavendish's film, Sonmi's declaration. The gap between Sonmi's execution and Zachry's valley is never specified beyond "after the Fall".
